summary: Soft, mashed-down beans served with a dark, smoky crushed-pepper sauce, often eaten with warm bread.
story: Ewa agoyin is a Lagos street food of soft, well-cooked beans with a dark, spicy sauce made from dried chillies fried in palm oil. It is commonly eaten with soft bread such as agege bread.

items.name: Dried chilli peppers or dried cayenne
Soft bread (agege or any soft loaf)

steps.title: Cook the beans
steps.text: Combine the beans, half the onion, oil and water in a large pot. Boil gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, topping up with hot water when needed. Beans are ready when they are completely soft and can be crushed easily between your fingers.

steps.title: Mash and thicken
steps.text: Add the salt, then mash a few spoonfuls against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon until the pot is thick and creamy while keeping some whole beans. Cook until most of the water has evaporated and the beans are moist, not soupy.

steps.title: Soak the chillies
steps.text: While the beans cook, soak the dried chillies in hot water for 10 minutes. Drain and blend coarsely, keeping some texture.

steps.title: Heat the palm oil
steps.text: In a heavy pan, heat the palm oil for 5 to 8 minutes over medium-low heat until it is very hot, darkens slightly and gives off a smoky aroma. Be careful of splatter.

steps.title: Fry the onions
steps.text: Add the sliced onions and fry slowly for 10 to 15 minutes until deep brown and almost caramelised. Add the iru for the last 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add the chilli
steps.text: Stir in the crushed chilli, crayfish and cube. Fry on low heat for 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce is very dark, almost black-brown, and the oil separates. Do not rush: it should smell rich and smoky, not burnt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the beans onto a plate, add a generous amount of sauce on top and serve with warm bread and plantain.

tips: Cook the sauce slowly. Rushing it makes it taste bitter.
Mash some beans but keep others whole for texture.
Soak the beans overnight to cut cooking time to about 1 hour.
Keep the sauce fiery. A drizzle goes a long way for mild eaters.

swaps.swap: Black-eyed peas or small brown lentils will cook faster and give a slightly different texture.
Use 1 1/2 tbsp ground cayenne or dried chilli flakes, fried briefly in the oil.
Omit or use a teaspoon of miso for savoury depth.

name: Ewa Agoyin
